title: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation

competencies.text: Propose adaptation and mitigation strategies for local biodiversity.
Evaluate overpopulation effects from secondary sources.

days.title: Adaptation vs Mitigation
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will propose adaptation and mitigation strategies to protect local biodiversity and evaluate the effects of overpopulation using secondary sources.

🔑 Two Kinds of Climate Action

MitigationAdaptation
GoalReduce the causes — cut greenhouse gas emissions or remove CO₂Reduce the harm from changes already happening
Question it answers"How do we warm the planet less?""How do we live safely with the change?"
ExamplesSolar and wind power, energy-efficient appliances, public transport, reforestation, less food wasteSeawalls, elevated houses, early-warning systems, drought- or flood-tolerant rice, rainwater harvesting

🌿 Some Actions Do Both

Mangrove restoration absorbs and stores carbon (mitigation) and shields coasts from storm surges while sheltering young fish (adaptation). Strategies that do both are especially valuable.

The Philippines' Climate Change Act of 2009 (RA 9729) created the Climate Change Commission, and LGUs prepare Local Climate Change Action Plans.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: A city replaces diesel buses with electric buses charged by solar power. This is mainly…

choices.label: Mitigation — it cuts greenhouse gas emissions
Adaptation — it protects the city from floods
Adaptation — it helps buses survive typhoons
Neither — transport has no link to climate

scenario.explanation: Reducing emissions addresses the cause of climate change, so it is mitigation.

scenario.text: A coastal town builds houses on stilts because floods are getting worse. This is mainly…

choices.label: Adaptation
Mitigation
Deforestation
Eutrophication

scenario.explanation: Elevated houses reduce harm from flooding that is already happening — adaptation.

scenario.text: Which strategy is BOTH mitigation and adaptation?

choices.label: Planting mangroves along the coast
Building only a concrete seawall there
Buying a larger air conditioner
Burning more coal for electricity

scenario.explanation: Mangroves store carbon (mitigation) and buffer storm surges and protect fish nurseries (adaptation).

days.title: Protecting Local Biodiversity
days.content:
🐠 Strategies That Work

StrategyHow it helps biodiversity
Marine Protected Areas (MPAs)No-fishing zones let fish grow and spill over to nearby fishing grounds (e.g., Apo Island)
Mangrove and forest restorationRestores habitat, stores carbon, protects watersheds
Wildlife corridorsConnect forest patches so species can shift ranges as climate changes
Seed banks and gene banksSave varieties (e.g., at PhilRice) for breeding climate-tolerant crops
Reducing other stressesLess pollution and overfishing make reefs better able to recover from bleaching

⚖️ Philippine Laws

  • RA 9729 — Climate Change Act (Climate Change Commission)
  • RA 9147 — Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act
  • RA 11038 — Expanded National Integrated Protected Areas System (E-NIPAS)
  • RA 10121 — Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each strategy or law to its description. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: Reducing the causes of climate change
No-take zone where fish populations recover
match.why: Apo Island is a famous example.

match.right: Connects habitats so species can move
Stores rain for the dry season

match.why: It created the Climate Change Commission.
It protects wild species and habitats.

match.right: Stores crop varieties for future breeding

days.title: Overpopulation and the Environment
days.content:
👥 Population Pressure

The Philippine population has grown past 110 million. More people need more food, water, housing, energy and transport. When demand grows faster than resources and planning, the environment suffers:

  • Habitat loss as forests and wetlands are cleared for farms and housing
  • More waste and pollution — garbage, sewage, air pollution in cities
  • Overfishing and overharvesting of reefs and forests
  • Higher emissions from energy use and traffic
  • Water stress and saltwater intrusion from over-pumping

📚 Evaluating Secondary Sources

A secondary source summarizes or interprets data collected by others — news articles, reports, textbooks. To evaluate one, ask:

  1. Who wrote it? Is the author or agency reliable (PSA, DENR, a university)?
  2. When? Is the data recent?
  3. Evidence: does it cite data, or only opinions?
  4. Bias: does it ignore other factors (consumption, technology, planning)?

Impact depends not only on the number of people but also on how much each person consumes and the technology used.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Propose and evaluate strategies. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: A coastal barangay in Ilocos floods yearly from stronger storm surges. Which adaptation is MOST suitable and lasting?

choices.label: Restore mangroves and set an early-warning plan
Cut nearby trees to let floodwater drain faster
Build more houses closer to the shoreline
Ignore it, since storm surges are rare events

scenario.explanation: Mangroves reduce wave energy and early warnings save lives — both adapt the community to stronger surges.

scenario.text: A town's population doubles in 20 years with no new sewage system. Which effect is MOST likely?

choices.label: More untreated wastewater polluting rivers
Cleaner rivers because people use less water
More forest cover because people move away
Less garbage because the town is crowded

scenario.explanation: More people produce more sewage; without treatment, it ends up in rivers, causing pollution and disease.

scenario.text: A blog says, "Overpopulation is the ONLY cause of environmental problems." How should you evaluate this claim?

choices.label: It is too simple — consumption and planning also matter
It is fully correct, since more people always means harm
It is reliable because blogs are always checked by experts
It is wrong, since population has no effect on nature

scenario.explanation: Environmental impact depends on population, consumption and technology. A claim that ignores these is biased or incomplete.

scenario.text: Metro Manila suffers both extreme heat and flooding. Which combination addresses BOTH mitigation and adaptation?

choices.label: More trees and parks plus better drainage and solar roofs
More private cars plus colder air-conditioner settings all day
Paving all open soil plus more coal power plants
Closing all parks plus building more malls

scenario.explanation: Trees cool the city and absorb CO₂; drainage reduces flooding; solar roofs cut emissions — a balanced plan.

scenario.text: A fishing community wants to restore declining fish catches. Which strategy is BEST supported by evidence?

choices.label: Set up a marine protected area with community rules
Use finer nets so more small fish are caught
Fish at night only, using dynamite to save much more time
Move all fishing boats to one small reef area

scenario.explanation: MPAs let fish grow and reproduce; their numbers spill over into nearby waters, raising catches over time.

days.title: Your Climate Action Plan
days.content:
📝 Building a Local Plan

  1. Identify the problem using data (e.g., more flooding each year in your barangay).
  2. Find the causes and who is affected, including plants and animals.
  3. Propose actions: at least one mitigation and one adaptation.
  4. Evaluate each action: Is it effective? Affordable? Fair to all? Does it harm other species?
  5. Plan to monitor results — for example, count fish or measure flood depth over time.

🏫 Example: School and Barangay

ActionTypeBenefit
Segregate waste; compost food scrapsMitigationLess methane from dumpsites
Rain barrels for school gardensAdaptationWater during dry spells
Plant native treesBothShade, habitat, carbon storage
Disaster drills and evacuation mapsAdaptationSaves lives during typhoons

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: What is the difference between adaptation and mitigation?

choices.label: Adaptation reduces harm; mitigation reduces causes
Adaptation reduces causes; mitigation reduces harm
They both mean planting trees in the mountains
Mitigation is only done by other countries abroad

escape.explanation: Mitigation cuts emissions (causes); adaptation adjusts to impacts (harm).

escape.text: Which is an example of MITIGATION?

choices.label: Installing solar panels
Building a seawall
Elevating a house
Typhoon early-warning sirens

escape.explanation: Solar power replaces fossil fuels and reduces emissions. The others reduce harm from impacts.

escape.text: Which law created the Climate Change Commission?
escape.explanation: RA 9729, the Climate Change Act of 2009, created the Climate Change Commission.

escape.text: Why does composting food scraps help mitigate climate change?

choices.label: Less food rots in dumpsites making methane
Compost releases extra oxygen into the air
Compost cools the soil and blocks sunlight
Compost turns carbon dioxide into plastic

escape.explanation: Food waste in dumpsites decays without oxygen and releases methane, a strong greenhouse gas.

escape.text: When judging a secondary source about overpopulation, which question is MOST important?

choices.label: Does it give reliable, recent data?
Does it use many colorful photos?
Is it written in very long sentences?
Was it shared by many people online?

escape.explanation: Reliable evidence and recent data matter most. Popularity and design do not make a source accurate.

escape.text: Which strategy BEST protects Philippine biodiversity as the climate warms?

choices.label: Connecting forest patches with wildlife corridors
Clearing forests to plant one crop over a wide area
Bringing in foreign species to replace native ones
Draining wetlands to build new subdivisions

escape.explanation: Corridors let species move to suitable habitats as conditions change, reducing the risk of local extinction.
